## 🔬 Research Identity
::: intro-block
**Imbalance-Aware AI · Urban Data Science · Reproducible AI Systems**

Jesús Cáceres-Tello is a researcher specialising in methodological artificial intelligence, with a focus on the evaluation of predictive models under real-world constraints in urban systems.

His work integrates urban sustainability, machine learning evaluation, and open computational science, with particular emphasis on class imbalance, temporal validation, and operational feasibility.

Rather than prioritising algorithmic novelty, his research emphasises:

```{=html}
<ul>
  <li><strong>Time-aware validation</strong></li>
  <li><strong>Performance–cost trade-off analysis</strong></li>
  <li>Methodological rigour</li>
  <li>Reproducibility by design</li>
  <li>Open science integration</li>
</ul>
```
:::

## 🎯 Research Mission
::: intro-block
The core objective of my research is to develop methodologically coherent AI frameworks for urban sustainability and STEM education.

This involves:

```{=html}
<ul>
  <li>Evaluating models under structural imbalance</li>
  <li>Designing reproducible analytical pipelines</li>
  <li>Integrating computational efficiency into model comparison</li>
  <li>Linking data science with institutional decision-making</li>
</ul>
```

My work contributes to a broader research programme in applied data science for sustainable systems, currently developed within my doctoral studies at the Complutense University of Madrid.
:::

## 🔬 Research Areas
::: intro-block
-   🌍 Urban environmental modelling and air quality forecasting
-   ⚖️ Imbalanced learning and classification evaluation
-   🤖 Hybrid predictive architectures (Prophet–LSTM, GAT–BiLSTM)
-   📈 Performance–cost trade-off analysis
-   🧩 Reproducible research and open science infrastructures\
-   🎓 AI-supported STEM education
:::

## 🏗 Research Infrastructure & Open Science
::: intro-block
All research projects are developed under a structured computational framework:

```{=html}
<ul>
  <li>Git-based version control</li>
  <li>Public repositories with DOI integration (Zenodo)</li>
  <li>Reproducible scripts and notebooks (R / Python / Quarto)</li>
  <li>Time-based validation strategies</li>
  <li>Transparent and standardised performance reporting</li>
</ul>
```

Each publication is accompanied by:

```{=html}
<ul>
  <li>An open repository</li>
  <li>Executable code</li>
  <li>Structured documentation</li>
  <li>Publicly accessible data sources</li>
</ul>
```

This framework ensures traceability, transparency, and methodological consistency across projects.
:::

## 🎓 Academic Background & Professional Experience
::: intro-block
Jesús Cáceres-Tello holds:

```{=html}
  <ul>
    <li>Ph.D. candidate in Data Science (Statistical Studies), Complutense University of Madrid  
        <em>(expected defence: April 2026)</em></li>
  
    <li>Master’s Degree in Artificial Intelligence, IoT and Big Data for Digital Transformation, INESEM Business School (2024)</li>
  
    <li>Master’s Degree in Educational Informatics, University of Alcalá</li>
  
    <li>B.Sc. in Information Systems Engineering, Catholic University of Ávila</li>
  
    <li>Diploma in Computer Science (Business Informatics), University of Málaga</li>
  </ul>
  
<p>His professional experience includes:</p>
  
  <ul>
    <li>Applied data science and artificial intelligence in public-sector environments (Madrid City Council)</li>
    <li>Participation in European and national research projects in health informatics and interoperability</li>
    <li>Development of data-driven systems, predictive models, and business intelligence solutions</li>
    <li>Leadership and coordination of digital infrastructure and analytics initiatives</li>
  </ul>
```

He has been teaching in higher education for over a decade and actively contributes to academic innovation initiatives.
:::
